gaps.why_now: The first honest Phase 14 landing is a dedicated build gate that keeps the workqueue boundary-map slice reviewable without pretending Zigux already owns live async execution.
A dedicated make target keeps the Phase 14 survey lane runnable with the same bounded discipline as the earlier tranche gates.
The existing export shim proves Zigux already has a reviewable kernel namespace foothold, so the workqueue lane can add a pure boundary map without inventing a fresh top-level layout.

The first honest `workqueue_bridge.zig` foothold is a boundary map around `queue_work_on()`, `__queue_work()`, `__alloc_workqueue()`, `cancel_work_sync()`, `manage_workers()`, and the rescuer or scheduler hooks, with explicit stay-in-C decisions where concurrency ownership is still too coupled to `worker_pool` state.
A dedicated Phase 14 gate is the smallest truthful way to lock the new boundary-map descriptor to the manifest and keep later runs from drifting into fake implementation claims.
The slice note records the exact boundary-map posture so the lane does not overstate symbol cataloging as a workqueue helper or execution bridge.
The survey note compares the 8,439-line `kernel/workqueue.c` anchor and its supporting header or test surfaces against the new boundary map so future runs stay honest about what still belongs in C.

The bridge now carries a small concurrency audit outline around `manage_workers()`, `struct worker_pool`, `wq_worker_running()` or `wq_worker_sleeping()`, and `rescuer_thread()` so Zigux can name `pool->manager`, forward-progress fields, scheduler-visible running state, and `pwq->mayday_cursor` without claiming live execution ownership.

The bridge now records the `__queue_work()` gate that chooses between `pool->worklist` and `pwq->inactive_works` while `max_active` and ordered-workqueue sequencing are still enforced under `pool->lock`, which is a reviewable field-level audit step before any wrapper claims live enqueue ownership. The same boundary keeps later `workqueue_set_max_active()` tuning honest by naming the inactive-list seam without moving it out of C.

The bridge now records the `__queue_work()` last-pool reentrancy handoff, the `process_one_work()` unlock and relock execution window, and the `worker_thread()` idle sleep transition so Zigux can name where `last_pool->lock`, `pool->lock`, and TASK_IDLE handoffs stay under C-owned concurrency control.

The bridge now records the irq-disabled PENDING-bit claim window across `try_to_grab_pending()` and `queue_work_on()`, plus the unbound `__queue_work()` `pwq->refcnt` retry loop, so Zigux can name pending ownership, retry, and reselection rules without claiming live submission control.

The bridge now records the `__flush_workqueue()` color cascade, `start_flush_work()` barrier insertion, and `pwq_dec_nr_in_flight()` release path so Zigux can name `wq->work_color`, `wq->flush_color`, `wq->first_flusher`, `wq->flusher_overflow`, and `nr_pwqs_to_flush` handoff rules without claiming live flush or cancellation completion.

The bridge now records how `drain_workqueue()` raises `__WQ_DRAINING`, loops back through `__flush_workqueue()` until each `pwq_is_empty()` check stabilizes, how `__flush_work()` waits on `barr.done` after `start_flush_work()` inserts a single-work barrier, and how `__cancel_work_sync()` only re-enables the work item after that wait path completes, so Zigux can name reflush and cancellation completion boundaries without claiming live draining or cancel parity.

The bridge now records how `__cancel_work()` folds `WORK_CANCEL_DISABLE` into `offqd.disable`, how `clear_pending_if_disabled()` keeps disabled work off-queue while clearing PENDING, how `__cancel_work_sync()` takes the disable path before choosing the BH warning versus `might_sleep()` and then flushes live execution, and how `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` reaches the same completion path with `WORK_CANCEL_DELAYED` set, so Zigux can name disable-depth and delayed-cancel boundaries without claiming live parity.

The bridge now records that `disable_delayed_work()` and `disable_delayed_work_sync()` are thin delayed-work aliases around `__cancel_work()` and `__cancel_work_sync()` with `WORK_CANCEL_DELAYED | WORK_CANCEL_DISABLE`, and that `enable_delayed_work()` routes through `enable_work()` to reopen queueability only when `offqd.disable` reaches zero, so Zigux can review delayed wrapper aliasing without claiming timer, execution, or requeue ownership.

The bridge now records that `queue_delayed_work_on()` and `mod_delayed_work_on()` are delayed-entry aliases over `__queue_delayed_work()`, that delayed submission keeps pending ownership on `work->data`, refuses disabled work instead of bypassing the existing off-queue disable state, and hands the item to `dwork->timer` until timer expiry re-enters `__queue_work()`, so Zigux can describe delayed submission routing without claiming CPU-affinity, timer-base, or requeue parity.

The bridge now records `delayed_work_timer_fn()` as the timer-expiry handoff back into `__queue_work()`, so Zigux can describe delayed timer ownership and requeue boundaries without claiming timer-base, CPU-affinity, or requeue parity.

Live worker_pool execution, pool draining, hotplug transitions, scheduler callbacks, rescue behavior, and forward-progress correctness remain blocked until the boundary map grows a tighter concurrency audit and Phase 14 still keeps those mechanisms in the existing C implementation.
